clue.text: United reported to be brilliant

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the clue word's synonym is heard rather than written

parts.note: knitted together means united or joined

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have been a dazzling player for United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported to be' signals that KNITTED (united) is said aloud, giving a rare word for shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitid is a literary word meaning bright, shining or lustrous.

clue.text: The only one of its kind uttered by a coiner

definitions.text: The only one of its kind
definitions.meaning: a term made up for a single occasion
said by someone who coins words, rather than one who forges money

explanation.surface: A forger mumbles about a unique item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coiner' looks like a counterfeiter, but here it is someone who coins new words.
explanation.definitionFit: A term invented for one occasion only is unique and is spoken first by its inventor.

clue.text: For a pick-me-up, go to the jug that's not finished

indicators.note: the slang word for prison stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: jug and nick are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: Feeling low, you could visit the jug before it is emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' suggests a pitcher of drink, apt for a pick-me-up, but it is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative drink or medicine that lifts the spirits.

clue.text: There is no expression for a departed god

parts.note: departed means dead
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: There is no word for a god who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'there is no term for', but describes a face with no expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker-faced look shows no emotion at all.

clue.text: Clemenceau's girl has dark spots

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: a plant that bears dark spots on its petals

parts.note: Georges Clemenceau, the French prime minister, was nicknamed 'the Tiger'
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The French statesman's daughter is said to have a blotchy complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: Clemenceau, French premier in the First World War, was known as 'le Tigre'. The definition describes the flower rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange lily species is known for the dark purple speckles on its petals.

clue.text: Epaminondas, for example, under the interdict

parts.note: an interdict is a prohibition, a ban

explanation.surface: A Greek general found himself prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: Epaminondas was a famous general of Thebes in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Epaminondas was a citizen of Thebes, so he is one example of its people.

clue.text: Dirck was one, Joris another

parts.note: two riders in Browning's poem about bringing the good news from Ghent to Aix on horseback at full speed

explanation.surface: A list of two Dutch names.
explanation.walkthrough: In Robert Browning's 'How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix', Dirck and Joris ride with the narrator at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider at full stretch on horseback, like the messengers in Browning's poem.

clue.text: Promotion for linesman who loses his touch

definitions.text: Promotion for linesman who loses his touch

parts.words: Promotion for linesman who loses his touch
parts.note: a touch judge or linesman runs the touchline; moving up means no longer watching touch but taking charge of the whole match

explanation.surface: A clumsy assistant official gets promoted anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a linesman is a touch judge; 'loses his touch' suggests failing skill but means leaving the touchline for the central role.
explanation.definitionFit: The match official in charge is the role above a linesman.

clue.text: I or Turpin can make forcible entry

indicators.note: these letters can be made into a new word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Dick Turpin the highwayman breaking into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a notorious English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: An irruption is a sudden violent bursting in.

clue.text: Mother turned sweet when Mandy changed places at the outset

indicators.text: Mandy changed places at the outset
indicators.note: read Mandy as M and Y: the letter M at the start gives way to Y

parts.note: mummy is a word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother grew affectionate when a girl called Mandy swapped seats at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandy' is not a girl but 'M and Y': Y takes the place of the first M.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy means delicious, sweet to the taste.

clue.text: Having no match for the type with six points

definitions.meaning: an old printers' name for a size of type of six points

explanation.surface: Nobody can rival this particular typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means peerless, and in old typesetting it also named a very small six-point type size.

clue.text: Reflection of the spirit of the tribunal

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the little word of is turned round

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Thinking about the spirit that animates a court of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection of' looks like a phrase about contemplation; 'Reflection' acts on the little word that follows it. A Roman forum also housed the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum was the Roman public square where courts sat, hence a court or place of judgment.

clue.text: Help a Gryphon lose the river race? Perhaps this would take a brainwave

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement among many, so the gathered letters are rearranged
the word race is told to lose the river abbreviation, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: Advice to the Gryphon from Alice in Wonderland about a boat race, then a joke about inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' takes R (river) out of RACE to leave ACE; 'Perhaps' then rearranges HELP A GRYPHON plus ACE. A brainwave here is literally an electrical wave from the brain, which the machine records.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical technique records the brain's electrical activity, so it would literally capture a wave from the head.

clue.text: Alumnus gets prolix, though not a square

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
prolix means long-winded, long

explanation.surface: A former pupil turns out to be wordy, though at least not a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like slang for a dull conventional person; it is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle with unequal sides is longer than it is wide, so it is not a square.

clue.text: Lecherous, perhaps, like Chris

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible rearrangement of the following letters

explanation.surface: A man named Chris may be a lecher.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickerish is an old word for lustful or greedy.

clue.text: Doing good cut short to make a living

indicators.note: the synonym for doing good loses its tail end, as something cut short does

parts.note: beneficence is the doing of good, active kindness

explanation.surface: Charity work curtailed so as to earn a wage.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a church post with an income, a sense far from earning one's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England a parish post with its income is called a living.

clue.text: See about unknown person summoned to court in agitation

indicators.note: about means around, so the cathedral city goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see
X is an unknown in algebra
cited means summoned to appear before a court

explanation.surface: Look at a stranger who has been called before the judge in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the bishop's diocese of Ely, an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, not the verb look.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in agitation means acting with nervous excitement.

clue.text: Short Dickens work containing example of envy

indicators.note: containing means the shortened novel holds another piece inside it

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge, a novel by Dickens, shortened to B Rudge
EG is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A brief Dickens novel full of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone is to resent or be jealous of what they have.

clue.text: Use key to unlock secret passage

definitions.text: Use key to unlock secret passage

parts.words: Use key to unlock secret passage
parts.note: reads like opening a hidden corridor with a key, but means using a code key to make an encrypted piece of text readable

explanation.surface: Someone opens a hidden tunnel with a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoding a ciphered text with its key makes the secret message plain.

clue.text: Bill may be stuck with his name on the back door

parts.note: a bill posted on a wall is a poster

explanation.surface: A notice pinned to a rear entrance bears the owner's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear gate or side entrance, especially in a castle.

clue.text: One runs the film back for the sake of peace

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: back asks for the word for film to be read in the other direction

parts.note: cine is a short word for film

explanation.surface: A projectionist rewinds the reel to keep things calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' acts only on the film word. The definition is adjectival in force: aimed at peace.
explanation.definitionFit: An irenic gesture is conciliatory, aimed at peacemaking rather than conflict.

clue.text: Recovered centre arms with suede arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement signals the letters are rearranged
centre takes the middle letters of the word arms

explanation.surface: Reupholstering the middle of an armchair with suede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' gives RM from ARMS; 'arrangement' shuffles RM with SUEDE. 'Recovered' tempts as reupholstered; it means taken up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Resumed means started again after a pause, carried on once more.

clue.text: High value, roughly speaking, he has to pay back

indicators.note: a rough, dropped-aitch way of speaking turns he's into 'e's

parts.note: he has contracts to he's

indicators.note: back reverses the word for paying

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone who must repay a debt is roughly valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly speaking' drops the H of HE'S, as in rough speech, to give ES; 'back' turns MEET into TEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, a great valuation of someone.

clue.text: Kind of flannels for a stonewaller?

definitions.meaning: trousers made of a fabric that does not wrinkle
a defensive cricketer who stubbornly holds out at the crease, the batting line

explanation.surface: Asking which trousers suit a dour defensive batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, flannels are white trousers, the crease is the line where the batsman stands, and a stonewaller is a batsman who blocks every ball rather than scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that won't wrinkle fits the trousers; a batsman defending stubbornly at the batting line is literally holding out there.

clue.text: "Have this dance!" said the wriggler

indicators.note: said means the wriggler's name is spoken, to be heard

parts.note: a conger is an eel, a wriggling creature

explanation.surface: An eel invites someone to join a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Eels wriggle, and the conger eel's name sounds like the Latin American line dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Cuban line dance with a kick on every fourth beat.

clue.text: Aside by a character

parts.note: a part in a play is a character

explanation.surface: An actor's whispered remark to the audience, delivered in role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aside' tempts as the actor's remark, fitting the theatre picture, but it is an adverb meaning separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart means set aside, separated from the rest.

clue.text: Sound recovery from a lesion

indicators.note: to recover is to get back, here taken as going backwards over the letters
the answer's letters are taken from within the words a lesion

explanation.surface: A medical note about getting well after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks ESION out of 'a lesion' and 'recovery' reads it backwards. 'Sound' wants to mean healthy, as after recovery; it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Medlar cooked and used in ideal country

indicators.note: cooked suggests the fruit's letters are worked over into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe using medlar fruit in some perfect land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges MEDLAR into DREAML, followed by AND as written. A medlar is a small brown fruit eaten when nearly rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A land of dreams is an imagined, perfect place.

clue.text: Club, originally glorified palace we hear

definitions.meaning: a London gentlemen's club of that name
in ancient Rome, a building where poets and scholars recited their works to listeners

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's club is said to have once been a grand palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the original Athenaeum of Hadrian's Rome, a hall where works were read aloud to be heard, named after the temple of Athena.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a London club derives from a Roman hall for recitals of literature, itself named after Athena.

clue.text: Half the code is cracked

definitions.meaning: full of dots, which make up half of Morse code alongside dashes

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have broken half a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse code is written in dots and dashes, so something made of dots is half of it. 'cracked' looks like codebreaking but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted with dots fits half of Morse; eccentric or slightly crazy fits cracked.
